title: Inspector / Debugger showing INCORRECT values for Integer type Variables.
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.4.1 Stable, and 4.4.1 Stable Mono downloaded from Godot's website. 

### System information

Windows 10 64 bit, AMD Ryzen 5 5600, Forward + rendering, 

### Issue description

Inspector AND debugger show INCORRECT _values_ for integer variables. 
The values of the variables are _correct in execution_, but **NOT in debugging scenarios**. 

### Steps to reproduce

**THIS IS NOT A GODOT STEAM ISSUE!** 

Using GodotSteam I did the following lines of code:
`var id : int = Steam.getSteamID()
var fauxname = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(id)
var fauxname_hc = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(76561197996072004)
var fauxname_hcO = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(76561197996072000)
var id32 = Steam.getSteamID32(id)
print("Steam ID : ", id, " to 32??? ", str(id32))`

In the attached screenshot you can see that the value of "id" ENDS in 2000 IN THE INSPECTOR...
However, when you get the steam username by passing the variable as an argument, it works correctly. 
When you hardcode the value into the argument it works correctly. 
**YET** when you hard code the argument to match the value in the inspector and debugger, the username is NOT returned appropriately. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/245c259e-5cce-4401-a705-e313f48743e0)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Godot 4.4.1
Steam with online internet connection. 
Download GodotSteam 4.4.1 from the "AssetLib" tab. 
Run the lines of code from above or also listed again here:
`var id : int = Steam.getSteamID()
var fauxname = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(id)
var fauxname_hc = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(76561197996072004)
var fauxname_hcO = Steam.getFriendPersonaName(76561197996072000)
var id32 = Steam.getSteamID32(id)
print("Steam ID : ", id, " to 32??? ", str(id32))`
